newsitem.title: USA: U.S corporate bonds lifted by Treasury rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S corporate bonds lifted by Treasury rally.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond prices were lifted by a strong rally in the Treasury market on Thursday, although trading volume remained moderate, market players said.
Prices on investment grade corporates followed Treasuries, causing spreads to remained unchanged. High-yield bonds rose by approximately 1/4 of a point.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose over one point on Thursday, ending the day at 98-27/32. The yield dropped to 6.59 percent.

Among specfic credits, ValuJet Airlines junk bond prices closed five points lower after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) stated that it would not grant approval for the airline to offer expanded service to West Palm Beach and Fort Myers, Florida.

An FAA spokeswoman said, "We are not permitting this expansion now becuase it is ValuJet's responsiblity to prove to the FAA that it is capable of safely operating the aircraft it has proposed to add to its fleet. To date it has not done so. We are continuing to review the request for expansion."

ValuJet has already sold 15,000 tickets for flights on the expanded routes and is now seeking FAA approval to arranging charter services with other airlines for passangers who own the tickets, the spokeswoman said.
Calls to ValuJet were not immediately returned.
MobileMedia Corp bonds tested new lows on Thursday on speculation that the paging company was going to declare bankruptcy imminently.
MobileMedia zero coupon bonds dropped to 20-24 from 25-27 1/2, a trader said. Its cash-pay bonds dropped to 30-34 from 35-38, he added.
